And as I said, they had logistics support from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And the HVO had a lot of logistics and a lot of support from the Republic of Croatia. And the 3rd Corps didn't have such a possibility. The main source of weapons for the 3rd Corps was capturing equipment from the aggressor in combat. That was the main way in which units of the 3rd Corps obtained weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to these questions about the map shown to you by the Prosecution, I'd just like to ask you to tell me your opinion, General, in the light of the factors you have just mentioned. Was the ABiH Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond superior in terms of strength in the area of Central Bosnia in comparison to its enemy?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The 3rd Corps wasn't superior in strength. It had more men, that is true. But in terms of the equipment that it had, in terms of its military equipment, it was in an inferior position. I've already mentioned the case of a brigade that should have had at least a hundred tanks, but it only had three to four tanks, whereas the aggressor had all the necessary weapons. I've already testified that weapons of the JNA were brought in from Slovenia and Croatia, these weapons were brought into the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was all under the control of the JNA, and the JNA certainly provided this equipment to the Republika Srpska Army. There were a lot of weapons. And I said before the war broke out the JNA was listed as the fourth most powerful force in Europe. The HVO was also very well equipped, very well armed. It was a modern force. They were supported by the Republic of Croatia. So when you take all these factors into consideration, then you see that the aggressor was more powerful. You should assess the strength of the force as a whole, not just in terms of its segments. If you try to assess the situation in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, one can draw that the conclusion that the 3rd Corps was in an inferior position in comparison to the aggressor and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You may now return to your seat. I have no further questions to ask you about the map. In response to a question from my learned colleague, page 12, lines 5 to 13 -- let me just check the date. It's the 13th of December. That's the date. You said that the 3rd Corps commander took numerous measures to train the units to ensure that they didn't violate international humanitarian law. You said that the men hadn't been militarily trained, and that the corps command took numerous measures if they established that a soldier was guilty. They took measures to punish such soldiers in an appropriate way. Do you remember testifying about this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, tell me, when it is more difficult to form army units, during war or in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in peacetime for sure. In wartime, it's extremely difficult to form units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. The second part of the sentence seems to contradict the first part. I wanted to know when it was more difficult to form units. And you, as far as I can see, answered in a slightly contradictory manner. Could you please clarify what you said. If you didn't understand my question correctly, my question was when it is more difficult to form a military unit. Is it more difficult to do so in wartime or in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it is more difficult to form a unit in wartime. This is quite normal. That is what I was saying. Perhaps you didn't understand my answer. In peacetime, it is easier to form a unit, whereas in wartime it is more difficult. This is the case in all armies, and this was the case in the 3rd Corps. That's why I said that that was quite normal. It's quite normal that it's more difficult to form units in wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by the Prosecution, you said that the men had no experience. Did this fact also have an influence on the difficulties that you encountered when forming units in wartime?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally. This is a very significant factor when it comes to forming units. If you have men who have been trained, who are able to carry out tasks, then it's easier. But if you have men who haven't been to military schools, who have no military experience, then it is far more difficult to form such units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to those difficulties that you had when it came to forming units because there was a war raging and the men hadn't been trained, tell me, the 3rd Corps commander and its organs, what did they do? What steps did they take if the men failed to obey orders or did not abide by the law?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim with full responsibility that the corps command and the 3rd Corps bodies took a number of measures when it was detected that some men had perpetrated crimes, or they took disciplinary measures in certain cases. These measures were taken at the level of control and command. I wouldn't rule out the possibility that some perpetrators were not discovered. But I can claim with full responsibility that when we discovered that someone had committed a crime, we really took measures to punish the perpetrator of the crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you tell me whether this was the policy followed by the supreme command staff, or was this just something accidental, or rather, do you know what the policy of the supreme command staff was with regard to men who had committed crimes or misdemeanors?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that the supreme command staff requested that all those who had committed crimes without exception be held to account. All those who had committed crimes were punished. And those were the policies followed within the 3rd Corps, too. There were no exceptions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given those policies followed in the 3rd Corps, do you know whether your commanders of subordinate units took such measures and obeyed your orders?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have already said that 3rd Corps policy also applied to subordinate units and brigade commanders, for example. We issued a number of orders in this respect, and according to the reports that we received from subordinate units, subordinate -- commanders of subordinate units followed the same policy that had been adopted by the 3rd Corps command. So they, too, suggested that all those who had committed errors be prosecuted. All those who had committed crimes or misdemeanors should be prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in the course of the cross-examination, my learned colleague said that failure to punish might have an effect on morale and the combat readiness of units. As a professional member of military, what would you say with regard to this suggestion made by the Prosecution? Would punishing men, in fact, have an effect on the morale and combat readiness of the units?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how I understood the question. This is just one factor that would have affected morale. To punish someone for a crime, that was the policy followed, and we punished all those who committed crimes. So this does affect morale, and this was one of the ways in which we attempted to improve morale within 3rd Corps units. But this wasn't done just for the sake of morale. This was done because we wanted to punish those who had perpetrated crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague also suggested the following, page 13, line 1 to 5. I will now paraphrase it. I'm mentioning this because the 3rd Corps leadership, including yourself and Commander Hadzihasanovic, took that duty very seriously. And this means that each report or any information on the perpetration of a crime was taken very seriously. My question is, as you were close to General Hadzihasanovic in 1993, could you say what attitude General Hadzihasanovic had towards the discipline of soldiers in general and towards prosecuting all those who had committed crimes or misdemeanors?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that my commander, General Hadzihasanovic, was very rigorous. He was a principled and consistent man. No exceptions were made when it came to men who had committed crimes or misdemeanors. He was very principled. And the fact that we knew each other had nothing to do with it. He followed principles. All I said was that I knew General Hadzihasanovic quite well. But I believe that he was very strict and rigorous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague also mentioned the events in Dusina today and earlier on. I have a few questions about that, but I would now like to tell you that General Reinhardt, a Prosecution witness, after having been informed of measures that were taken in Dusina said that he thought that General Hadzihasanovic had taken all the necessary measures with regard Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond to the events in Dusina. General, would you agree with what General Reinhardt stated before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the fact that General Reinhardt made such an assessment, but I have already stated on the basis of my information that General Hadzihasanovic did everything that he could with regard to Dusina. Everything that was within his remit, and I agree with the assessment made by General Reinhardt.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the measures taken, could the witness be shown DH155/3. Since we have enough time, could we have three documents, DH155/3, DH155/2, and DH119.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, please have a look at DH155, document 3. It's from the ABiH, 3rd Corps, the military police battalion. And it's a document from 1993. Do you have that document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under item 1, or rather, first of all, the subject of this document is a report from the military police battalion for the month of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. We'll first have a look at the document since we don't have it. Could you please show us the document. We'll need the English version. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I'm referring to DH155/3. It's a report for August 1993. It's from the military police battalion dated the 3rd of September 1993. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I have seen what you have just read out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first title is to do with the focus of engagement for the military police battalion. Please have a look at paragraph 1 and tell me whether as deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, you were aware of the fact that what is mentioned under item 1 were, in fact, the duties carried out by the military police battalion at the time of this report.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, tell me, do you know whether battalion members were engaged in combat when necessary?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a look at item 2, participation in combat, tell me whether this indicates that military policemen were engaged in August in combat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please pay attention to item 3 now. And could you please read out what it says under (A).

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3(A) states the following: 22.700 members of the ABiH and civilians were identified or registered when controlling motor vehicles and when checking individuals on patrols and at checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you tell me whether checking the papers of individuals was a regular task that the military police had, and was this one of the ways in which they attempted to prevent crimes from being perpetrated, especially as far as stealing vehicles and property is concerned?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was one of the measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under (B), could you read out what it says under (B).

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the premises of the military police battalion, 256 individuals have been detained up until 10.00. And after 10.00, 25 individuals were detained since it was permissible to do so for a 24-hour period of time."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to ABiH members, how many ABiH members were brought in in that month?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says 268 ABiH members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under (D), can you tell me how many members of the military were detained in that month alone?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it says 50 individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, have a look at item 4, criminal reports and reports on misdemeanors. Could you just read out item (A), the first two lines in item (A).

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: (A), to the military prosecutors court, 24 criminal reports were filed against 32 individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, given your testimony, does this report from the military police battalion show the numerous measures that were taken against ABiH members?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms my testimony to date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at Document DH155/2 now. This is also a document from the military police dated the 20th of March 1993. It's a report on the criminal reports filed. Can you tell me which period this report refers to. Under (A), does it mention the period concerned by the military police report?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The period concerned is the end of 1992, and 1993, and the first two months of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document also refers to the number of criminal reports filed during that period.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that "total of 377 criminal reports were filed."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under (B), it also says -- it also mentions the number of individuals against whom criminal reports were filed.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here it says that reports were filed for 804 identified and 20 unidentified perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, does this document which refers to the work of the military police battalion, does this document conform to the policies followed by the 3rd Corps with regard to prosecuting perpetrators for crimes?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms what I have testified about, and this is what it states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In line 20, page 53, it says 20 March 1993. It may have been my slip of the tongue. The date, however, is 20 March 1994. Can you please look Document DH119. This is a document from the district military prosecutor in Travnik. Again, the year is 1994.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you can see in this document, this is the report on the work of the military prosecutor's office in Travnik for the year 1993. Is that the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document that I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll kindly ask you to look at page 2 of this document under II, item 2, this is "received criminal reports." Can you see how many reports were filed in 1993 and against how many perpetrators all together?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "the prosecutor's office in the reporting period received a total of 823 criminal reports against 1.044 persons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this information in the report, is this a result of the policies that were established by the 3rd Corps and refer to all the perpetrators of crimes and misdemeanors?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On line -- on page 15, lines 3 to 8 on the 13th of this month, in response to the Prosecutor's question, you were talking about your relationship with the international organisations. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I was talking about my relationship with the international organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you ever refuse to meet with a representative of the international organisations and talk to them?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before this Court, I have testified that I never turned down cooperation with any of the international organisations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although one part of your duties as deputy commander was liaison with the international organisations, especially within the scope of the Musalac commission and later on the commission in Vitez and in Travnik, my next question is as follows: What was the relationship and attitude of Commander Hadzihasanovic towards international organisations? Was he also willing to meet with them whenever possible to talk to them on any issue? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very often, together with my commander, General Hadzihasanovic, in a position to talk to international organisations. As far as I know, General Hadzihasanovic never refused cooperation with international organisations. To the contrary, I believe that his cooperation was really good. My commander was always willing to provide information requested by the international community, although sometimes there were problems involved in that because some members of international organisations could not always appreciate the role and the position of the 3rd Corps commander with regard to his obligations and commitments. Sometimes these people from international organisations were not happy with the answers provided to them by General Hadzihasanovic. I, however, know that General Hadzihasanovic received all the international organisations and provided all of them with all the information requested from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you've also testified that you would most often use the services of the international community, that is, the BritBat, when you travelled around the area. What were the reasons that compelled you to travel around the area, and how did you travel?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already testified about that before this Court. I said that I moved through the area of combat operations, and the only way one could move through those areas was in BritBat vehicles. Why is that? Those were armoured vehicles which were safe, and these are the vehicles that are used to travel to the meetings of the joint commission, of the joint command, to the meetings organised by the international community in any of the locations. I also had the vehicle of the 3rd Corps at my disposal, and I used it whenever I could. Whenever a road was made passable, I would use that vehicle to inspect my units. At the request of the joint commission, I visited the places which were suggested as being problematic by the HVO or the international community. And this I did in the BritBat vehicles. I used my own vehicle to inspect my units in order to see how orders were carried out in those units and to receive reports from those units, or to check the reports from those units that had arrived at the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when you travelled the area with the help of the international community or within the scope of your duties, how did you go? Were you armed? Did you have any communication means?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never carried arms to those meetings and to those inspections. I never had a radio set on me which would allow me to maintain constant communication with the superior command. Not because I didn't want to carry one, but we did not have enough of them. I thought it was more important for fighters on the front line to have arms than for me, deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier today, the Prosecutor asked you whether UNPROFOR or the international community were prevented from passing through certain checkpoints manned by the BiH Army. Tell me, what was the principal policy of the 3rd Corps with regard to the international community and allowing them passage through the area of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 3rd Corps, we issued orders to allow for an unobstructed passage to the international organisations. Whenever we received information that there might be problems, we would deal with those problems immediately. Either somebody from the corps command went to that place to see what the problem was all about. I mentioned a case which I remember very well when I had to intervene in Karcuni in Busovaca Municipality. This was in January 1993. I've described that incident before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the general now be provided with P13 [as interpreted] and P644. This will allow me to put some additional questions to the general. On line 1, it says P13, and it should be P133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have P644, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you look at both of these documents and read them. They're not long, and they both bear the same date, 26 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have P644. I don't know what the other document is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is P133.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the two documents before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have P133 as well?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have P133.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well then. Can you please read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. Don't read out loud. Read them to yourself, and I'll ask you questions. One is from the HVO and one is from the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I'll read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the second paragraph of the 3rd Corps document and the first paragraph of the HVO document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, can you see that in both documents, a reference is made to the fact that Colonel Blaskic at the meeting said that there had been some killings during the negotiations about the prisoners from Lasva. This is the army document. The HV document says that Zvonko Rajic and three soldiers went to Lasva, and they were killed during the negotiations, which shows the character of the aggressor. My question, General, is as follows: At the moment when Colonel Blaskic was leaving the meeting, did he tell you that this is exactly what had happened, that some negotiators were killed? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that he said that. I don't think that he said that negotiators had been killed. He did not make a reference to any negotiators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you reported to the corps commander what happened during the meeting, how come that this is contained in the commander's report since you were the one who reported to him on the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that the press service of the Croatian Defence Council published something that was not said at the meeting in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you have any information about that incident, any combat report, any subsequent information that spoke about any negotiations and about these negotiators having been killed? Did anybody confirm that while you were reviewing the situation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody ever said that to me. I never, ever read anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it had been said by the -- by Colonel Blaskic or if this is contained in any of the HVO documents, there was no way for you to verify this information?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the cross-examination, my learned friend asked you whether you knew Serif Patkovic and whether you spoke to him about the events in Dusina. You have answered that question. And my question is as follows: The company of the 7th Muslim Brigade which was in the area of Dusina at the moment, was it on the strength of the 2nd Battalion or was it at that moment resubordinated to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read that order, and I remember that the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was resubordinated to the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Zenica Municipality for this particular task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have also told us that the municipal staff was involved in the investigation. Is it normal in military sense that a unit to which a unit used in combat is resubordinated is involved in the investigation of the things that happened during combat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is normal. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked whether you read any subsequent reports that would possibly mention Serif Patkovic. With regard to your testimony before the cantonal court in Zenica, are you aware of the fact that the late Rajic's wife was heard before that court?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I testified about the events in Dusina, which involved a person called Edin Hakanovic. No reference was made to any person called Milica at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know what the lady's name is, whether it is Milica or something else, but since you are not familiar with that, I will not insist on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe this would be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much more do you need for the re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not more than half an hour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We will adjourn, and we will resume at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed -- well, will resume as soon as the accused are here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I will first ask you this: As you have answered to one of my questions that you needed medical assistance yesterday, are you feeling all right now? May I continue with questions?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you may continue with questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, if you don't feel well, just tell us. If you feel ill, don't feel well at all, we'll just stop the hearing, because I can see you don't look that well. You're all pale. Are you okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm feeling all right. Of course I'm not quite myself, as I'm testifying here before this Honourable Chamber. I'm trying to be as precise and accurate as possible, but don't worry; I've been through worse situations in my life. And should I feel that I cannot continue, I will inform you. Thank you for the concern you have shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll keep an eye on it and we'll see whether it is necessary to stop the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when asked by my learned friend, the Prosecutor, on page 21, line 1 through 17, you spoke about the Patriotic League and your membership in the Patriotic League. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, General, in addition to the Patriotic League, were there any other patriotic groups being established during the war in Central Bosnia and in the wider area? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already partially answered this question. You can check my previous answers. I said that in the beginning of the war there were some people with patriotic orientation who got organised in order to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina. And there were various groups that existed under various names and that had this orientation. There was the Patriotic League, then there was a group called the Green Berets. Then there were groups called Bridge and Green Legion. There were a number of other groups with various names. I cannot recall all of them. I already stated that I myself was a member of the Patriotic League and that I could give you more information about the Patriotic League if you're interested. And the Prosecutor asked me a number of questions about the Patriotic League and I answered to the best of my abilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, please tell us based on the information you had at the time, what was the main objective, the main goal, of these patriotic forces, patriotic organisations that existed under various names as you have stated?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to be as precise as possible before this Honourable Chamber, therefore I will tell you these are groups of people with patriotic orientation. This does not involve a large group of people, at least as far as I know. The goal of the Patriotic League was to prepare the patriots in order to respond to the aggression in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We received through the media information about how difficult the situation was, what difficulties Bosnia was facing, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when answering the questions of my learned friend and also now when answering my questions, you have always provided us with the information that you have about the Patriotic League. Is it because you yourself were a member of this patriotic group?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I was a member of this patriotic group; I'm not denying that. And that was before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, as you have stated several times -- and it is your task as witness here to tell us what you know, to provide all the information you have about this structure of these patriotic groups -- can you give us information only about the Patriotic League, whose member you were, or can you tell us something about the organisation and structure of these other groups of whose existence you knew?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke before this Honourable Chamber only about the Patriotic League. I can provide information only about that organisation, not about other organised groups with patriotic orientation. I know there was also an organisation called HOS, H-O-S, which was also a group of patriots. But I cannot speak about other organisations. I can only tell you what I know about the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you also told us when the decision was made to put the patriotic groups under the command of the Territorial Defence you personally and other members of the Patriotic League, joined the Territorial Defence. My question is: When you joined the Territorial Defence and later on the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was that something that happened at one point in time only, or was this a process? Or rather, did all the people join the Territorial Defence or there were some individuals or groups that continued existing outside of the Territorial Defence after this period?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, I can only testify about the Patriotic League, not about other groups. After the decision of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to pace all patriotically oriented forces under the newly established Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I know that this issue was resolved within the Patriotic League itself. Immediately after that we went to the Territorial Defence and placed ourselves under the command of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But naturally, this was a process that took some time. This is not something that happened in one or two days. I know that there were some individuals from the Patriotic League who believed that it was not yet time to join the Territorial Defence, that the time was not ripe yet. They thought that this was the Territorial Defence of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, whether still existed some influence of the former Yugoslav People's Army [as interpreted]. I cannot tell you what the situation is regarding other organisations, when they joined the Territorial Defence and so on. I can only testify about the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. My learned friend asked several questions of you concerning mujahedin and how you dealt with these armed foreigners who found themselves in the territory of the 3rd Corps. When answering the Prosecutor's questions, you basically testified about what you knew about the foreigners depending on the period in question. So please tell us now, what information do you have about the stay of those foreigners in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina before the kidnapping of Zivko Totic and with respect to the 3rd Corps as a military force whose mission was to defend the territory, did they foreigners represent a problem for the 3rd Corps and did you pay any special attention to them?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave many answers to the Prosecutor on that question. They put a lot of questions to me regarding that. All I can tell you is that before the kidnapping of the Major of the HVO, who as we later found out was kidnapped by those foreigners, until he was kidnapped I personally and also the commanding staff did not see this as a big problem until this man was kidnapped, because these foreigners were not members of the 3rd Corps. They were foreigners, and we didn't know how they arrived in that territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, when asked by my learned friend you provided exactly that answer, namely that it was foreigners who were involved in the kidnapping of Zivko Totic and that when that happened you realised that that was a problem. Please tell us this: As commander of the 3rd Corps, do you know whether immediately upon learning of this problem was your superior command informed about it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, on the day of the kidnapping of the officer of the HVO, we did not have information about the culprits. I know civilian police were involved in it and they were assisted by the military police. Basically everybody was involved in dealing with this. This was quite a peculiar event. That was the first time that the officers of the HVO were kidnapped. Naturally that represented a problem for us. As far as I remember, the first information to the effect that it had been done by the foreigners came from the European monitors, therefore from an international organisation. And I've testify about that already here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, General, was this: When you received that information from the international community several days following the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, did you immediately thereafter inform your superior command about that problem?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I had a different task. Within the command of the 3rd Corps, there was information that there had been a kidnapping; however, the 3rd Corps didn't know who was responsible for the kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the Prosecutor showed you minutes from a meeting. You spoke about that meeting in examination-in-chief. That was the meeting held on the 23rd of April in late evening hours. Please tell us: Was that the first time that you mentioned to your commander, as far as you know, the problem involving the foreigners?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, on the 21st or 22nd of April a meeting was held at the command headquarters when we -- when they discussed for the first time the problem involving foreigners, definitely after the kidnapping of Zivko Totic. However, already at that time we at the 3rd Corps had the information available to us. I'm not sure on what day exactly we received information from the European Monitoring Mission about the fact that the kidnapping had been carried out by the foreigners and that they had some contact with the foreigners. I think that this information arrived before this meeting held on the 21st April of 1993 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the presence of these armed foreigners represented a serious problem and that you became aware of that after the murder that they had committed in Miletici. In view of this testimony of yours please tell us: Do you know whether at the time within the BH army any steps were being taken in order to respond to a number of questions relating to the foreigners? And you gave evidence about this this morning.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps did take steps and measures. I spoke about these measures here. After the events in Miletici, we realised that the problem was growing, becoming more significant, also based on the statements of the residents of Miletici who claimed that the crimes and murders had been committed by the so-called mujahedin, as they called them at the time, the foreigners. Therefore, it was entirely clear to us that there were no members of the BH army present there and that we didn't have to investigate anything in particular at the time. Therefore, our activities, the activities of the 3rd Corps, did not change in any respect; however, I spoke a lot about this when asked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has just drawn my attention that in the English translation in 9:13 it says "our activities," whereas the French interpretation was faithful to what the witness said, and the witness said "our principal mission," and I would like this to be recorded in the English text as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, General, that it was clear that those were not members of the BH army involved. If I can paraphrase something that you said several times, you had responsibilities and competency for investigating only members of the army. Let me ask you: Did you have a legal responsibility as an army, as the corps, to investigate the case of these mujahedin or did you take the measures that you mentioned just because you perceived a problem that was harming the reputation of the army despite the fact that it did not originate from the army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said yesterday that we as the corps did not have the legal obligation to take any legal action against that group, but we did believe that that group was damaging the reputation of the 3rd Corps. And although we did not have the legal obligation to investigate cases not involving members of the BH army, and let me clarify this, we only had the legal obligation to investigate in cases involving BH army members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a Prosecutor's question you said that some services took some operative measures. Tell me, as a member of the profession, is it normal that before gaining an image about the problem in its entirety you first tried to gather all the underlying information?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's very important. We had to gather, if not all information then at least as much as possible. An important decision cannot be made without a great deal of information. In that job, like in any job, it is important to have a great deal of information in order to make such a decision. An uninformed decision could be catastrophic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 69, line 12, my colleague again warns me that "operative measures" as it reads in the English text does not make much sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would therefore like to ask you to clarify. What does "operative measures" actually mean in terms of security?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean surveillance imposed on certain people; attempts to infiltrate the group of that people by a member of the security organ; cooperation with civilian police; cooperation with the local population with the aim of detecting, exposing, those people; all efforts to gather as much information as possible. As a person who does not strictly belong to that profession, that's all I can tell you. Maybe that also involves wiretapping and some other measures, but that's the most precise answer I can give you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked on page 11 of the transcript from the 14th December relating to your visit to Guca Gora together with ECMM monitors and Fra Stipan Radic. Let me ask you: Was this monastery standing intact, more or less, when you visited it or was it destroyed or damaged in some other way?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not destroyed by any means. I said that the foreigners attempted to destroy it, but they didn't. It bore signs only of minor damage. I don't know what Mr. Fra Stipan Radic said, whether he was happy with the situation that he saw, but I didn't see any major visible damage. I only mentioned the damage that I could notice. The monastery was not destroyed. It wasn't burnt, the walls were intact, not even windows or doors were broken. And I could only mention the little bit of damage that I could see in the room I went in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you live in Bosnia, and as all of us at some point you entered various temples, Catholic, Orthodox, or Muslim. When you entered this monastery, was it in such a state that a religious service could immediately take place in it? Otherwise, that it could immediately serve its purpose as a building with the help of the competent priests?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not particularly competent to speak on the subject, especially with regard to Catholic places of worship, but I believed then and I believe now that it was possible to hold a prayer at that time, that Catholic believers were able to use it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned, General, a piece of evidence you gave before, namely that the foreigners had told you that they wanted to destroy the building. On the 3rd of August when you found yourself before that building that was intact and was fit to serve its purpose, were you satisfied with the fact that your efforts helped preserve that building for your Catholic fellow citizens and all the other citizens? Were you personally satisfied that you had taken all those measures that you have already testified about?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already gave evidence that I have always tried and even drawn up documents at the time when General Hadzihasanovic was absent to the effect that special attention should be given to the preservation of the places of worship. I know from the history of the Bosnian people, including Bosnian Catholics, that this monastery was very important and I was therefore very happy to make my own contribution to preserve this monastery. And I am very happy that it is still standing there. That monastery is part of the culture of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not only Catholics but the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I'm proud of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, can you remember whether Fra Stipan Radic, Father Stipan Radic, expressed his view on the fact that the army was helping preserve the monastery?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a good and close relationship with Father Stipan Radic and I always accepted his suggestions and was ready to help in similar situations. I don't know what he said in my absence or what he may have said, but in my presence he said that he was very happy that the monastery was saved from destruction, that it was intact, and maybe as a person who is of Catholic faith and a Catholic priest he was in a position to notice damage, if any, better than I was. And if he was happy, then I was happy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my learned friend asked you a question about the establishment of the El Mujahed unit, but I would like to ask you this: After the establishment of the El Mujahed unit was the problem of the foreigners resolved? In 1993 did they place themselves under the control and the command of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoken about this at length and I will only remind you once again that with the writing of that order placing them under the control and command of the corps, the problem itself was not revolved. I mentioned that several orders were written, that in particular situations they should be resubordinated or committed in a particular action. Our experience with them was not always good. I remember that we had a very negative experience when they refused. And our commander commented that they were not fit for fighting, that they were responsible for a great number of casualties in that particular operation. And as I already said, the problem of the El Mujahed unit, the problem of the foreigners, was not resolved by the establishment of that unit. Many other attempts were made and many other problems were encountered later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you continued in the course of 1993 to perceive problems, tell me, General, did you warn about that your superior command and did those problems require the direct involvement of the superior commander?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I remember the problem remained even in 1994. I remember even the chief of staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Rasim Delic, came to a meeting to discuss it. Activities were undertaken to place those foreigners under control, at least within the system of regulations of the BH army. And if they don't want to comply -- those who don't want to comply, they should turn in their passports and IDs. Some of them refused. I already testified about this. Maybe twenty of them refused and they were expelled eventually from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As far as I know it was the civilian police, or rather the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina that expelled them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, on page 56 of the transcript of the 14th of December, the Prosecutor asked you why you failed to suggest a cease-fire to the HVO in order to resolve the problem with the mujahedin. Tell me, as a career officer, would it have been normal for you to suggest a cease-fire to the enemy in order to resolve the problem, even if it were mutual, and then to resume hostilities? Is that something commonly done in relations between two hostile armies?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to numerous questions of my learned friend yesterday and today, you answered why exactly you were unable to take military action against the mujahedin. I don't want you to repeat what you said before, that you didn't know their number, their objectives, you didn't know how they had come, what weaponry they had at their disposal. My question would rather be: Regardless of how that problem continued to aggravate, were you able to continue performing your basic mission -- would you have been able to perform your basic mission if you had to be side-tracked and concentrate on resolving the problem of the foreigners?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said, we could not afford to allocate the necessary resources because that would have impoverished our defence lines and it would have undermined the basic mission of the 3rd Corps. I think still that it was more important to defend the territory from the aggressor, which was hovering over us like a predator. We simply couldn't afford to open up a third front line. We didn't have enough personnel or materiel. I already mentioned that we had fighting men with 10 to 15 rounds per barrel and an expert would understand that this is nothing if you have to face an enemy in combat. Any soldiers who knows the first thing about the army would understand that it would have been catastrophic at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This morning in response to the Prosecutor's question you said, General, that precisely because you were unable to assess the problem properly, you sought assistance from the superior command. Is it normal for a soldier to seek assistance from a superior command; in other words, is it normal, regular, to seek the definition of a clear assignment after gaining a picture of all the elements that form this assignment?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is perfectly normal and logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of various and varying numbers of foreigners in that area and their link with the local population, tell me, is it in dispute that any military action would have also caused casualties, both on the side of the BH army and on the side of the local population?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certain that there would be great losses incurred both to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to the citizenry of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As commander of the 3rd Corps could General Hadzihasanovic have undertaken such a military operation without previously having obtained the agreement from the supreme command staff who would have been aware of the consequences of such measures?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite normal in the system of command and control of all armies, and that's the case for the ABiH as well. If the subordinate command can't resolve the difficulty, then they ask for assistance from the supreme command, the superior command. And then it's the duty of the superior command to help, to take measures to assist its subordinate unit; that is the superior command's duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to be a little more precise, General, could Commander Hadzihasanovic engaged in a military operation that would have entailed a significant number of military and civilian casualties without authorisation from his superior command to engage in such an action?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Hadzihasanovic couldn't have undertaken any such action at the time without having obtained the authority of his superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, tell me now, in the light of your military experience and the fact that you have experience of war as well, which is probably not the case for many generals, tell me whether a military commander, when confronted with a given problem -- well, first of all, tell me what is the attitude of a military commander? Does such a commander try to resolve the problem by using force? Does he accept the fact that there will be casualties? Or does such a commander try to resolve the difficulty without having recourse to force -- without risking the lives of men?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that all commanders should try to resolve problems without placing the life of anyone at risk. I think that each commander considers the lives of his soldiers to be valuable as well as the lives of civilians. So any commander or corps commander, too, doesn't want to sustain casualties for no reason. That is why such a commander believes the life of all soldiers and all citizens are valuable and that it is his duty to defend them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This general attitude that military commanders have, was this also the attitude of the 3rd Corps command and was it your personal attitude?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my personal attitude. And as far as I know, that was the attitude of my commander, too. That was the attitude of Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, I believe that was his position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have been asked additional questions that relate to the kidnapping of the HVO officer -- of HVO officers and to the kidnapping of Zivko Totic. Answering my questions and the Prosecution's questions you said that the 3rd Corps commander, whenever he found out or suspected that his men had committed certain acts, he would take certain measures, he would take the appropriate measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness P899, P857, and P194. In order to save time we have copies of these documents which we will submit to the Trial Chamber and to my learned colleagues. We've prepared copies of these exhibits, so perhaps it's not necessary to look for the documents for the Chamber and for my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that the documents you are showing to the witness relate directly to the Totic affair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to the kidnapping of four HVO officers who were later exchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you remind us of the date when the four HVO officers were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the 13th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how is a document dated the 26th of June, 1993, related to the Totic affair?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why you have been provided with that document, Mr. President. I was referring to document P194.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you mentioned document 194, and that also concerns P899, which is dated the 25th of January. The kidnapping took place on another date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I made a mistake. I mentioned documents P857, P899, and P194. We have made a sufficient amount of copies for the Chamber, for the witness, and for my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects to this as not arising out of cross-examination. The witness was asked questions about these affairs during direct examination. And although I did ask him some questions about it during the cross-examination, it is certainly not something that arose for the first time during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my learned colleague put a number of questions about going to Ravno Rostovo. That is the only place where these four captured HVO officers were sought for, so I don't know how it's not related. It's related to when the Prosecution asked the witness about it and it's related to the witness's answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Which document is concerned then? Which document relates to the event?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would first like to refer to the 3rd Corps command document dated the 13th of April, 1993. This order was forwarded to the Zapad Operations Group and it says that in the course of the 3th of April, 1993, HVO members were kidnapped and then an order was issued and it was said that it was suspected that they had gone in the direction of Ravno Rostovo and they said together with an HVO a patrol should be formed in the Ravno Rostovo area and the facts should be established. The following document is dated the 14th of April, and the command of the Zapad OG orders his subordinate units in this document to carry out this order of the 3rd Corps commander. And in document P899 dated the 15th of April, 1993, refers to the report from subordinate commands of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, have you had a look at these two documents?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found these documents. I found the document from the 3rd Corps command dated the 30th of April. Yes [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got the document dated the 14th of April, P857?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: P857, yes, I have that document, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document sent by Selmo Cikotic. It's a 3rd Corps document. Do you have a report P899, which is a report dated the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have those three documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Prosecution you said that you went to Ravno Rostovo as part of the mixed commission and together with European monitors. The documents that I have just mentioned and that I have provided you with, do these documents also refer to the measures that the 3rd Corps command immediately took to show that they wanted to investigate the suspicion that the HVO had that the ABiH had committed the act?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is shown in the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you said whenever the 3rd Corps believed that its members had committed certain acts they would go together with the HVO to the relevant location to investigate everything that had to do with the case. Do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What the 3rd Corps command did with regard to the allegation that ABiH members had kidnapped these men shows that the 3rd Corps command took such matters very seriously. Whenever they were informed of such events, whenever they were informed that such ABiH members may have committed certain acts they took this seriously and tried to shed light on this act. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to save time, General, it would be best for me to put the question to you now. In fact we have three documents that concern the kidnapping of the four officers, and their names are provided, obviously. There was an immediate reaction to this kidnapping. As far as you can remember, do you remember similar documents when Totic was kidnapped? Did you see documents of this kind that referred to Mr. Totic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already spoken about the fact that my main task involved performing duties that I have in the joint commission, and I have -- I have no information about all the documents sent by the 3rd Corps command. I don't know whether they sent such documents, but I know that whenever the corps command had information according to which ABiH members were suspected of having committed a crime, I know that in such cases the 3rd Corps command would immediately take measures, and this included orders issued to subordinate units to investigate the matter. If the event took place in the unit's zone of responsibility. I also said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have all understood that well, but my question was very specific. We have three documents here that relate to four HVO officers, at the time, in April. Were you familiar with these documents that related to these four officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found out about that at a meeting of the joint commission when the subject was discussed by Franjo Nakic, who was a member of the joint commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And with regard to Totic, did the 3rd Corps issue orders requesting that the units take the same steps referred to in these three documents? I'm referring to the Totic case now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I know, no one ever said that they suspected that 3rd Corps members had been involved in the act. In the case of the kidnapping of these officers of the HVO, it was said that they suspected that ABiH members were involved in this kidnapping. I don't know whether the 3rd Corps command immediately drafted orders, but at the time I know that no one suspected that members of the 3rd Corps had kidnapped Totic. No one expressed such an idea, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, without suspecting anyone there might have been an order stating that an HVO officer had been kidnapped by unknown men and all the units, including the military police, were requested to mobilise in order to try and find the person or those who had kidnapped a high-ranking officer. As far as you know that was done or wasn't done? Because if there were such documents one would see them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I must provide you with a more lengthy explanation. I said on returning from Vitez I went to the Hotel Internacional, where I found out that Zivko Totic had been kidnapped. At that meeting it was said that the civilian police should be responsible for the affair and I set off on another mission. On a number of occasions I have testified here that the civilian and military police cooperated. And as a result I did not notice that the corps command had drafted such documents. I didn't notice they drafted the kind of documents they had drafted in the case of the kidnapping of these three, or rather, four kidnappings in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you told us you were on your way to Zenica when you found out about the meeting in the Internacional Hotel. Can you remember now who attended the meeting, representatives of which organs, and what was discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend the meeting from the very beginning. I don't know at which stage of the meeting I entered the room where it was held. However, representatives of civilian organs of authority were present there. I know that there was a representative of civilian police attending the meeting as well. I realised that the main discussion was in progress or nearing its conclusion when I entered the discussion concerning the kidnapping regarding Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that civilian police was in charge of the main task. Can you tell us whether the military police, or rather the corps also took upon itself certain responsibilities? And also do you know whether they carried out these responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, the military and civilian police cooperated in all cases. I don't have any reliable information. I cannot corroborate this with documents, however it is a fact that they cooperated and I believe they cooperated on this case as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P411. P411.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I will ask you to read out paragraph 3. Please put it on the ELMO and then you can read it out and the interpreters will interpret that. The bit that begins at "around 9.00."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I just read out this paragraph beginning with "at around 0900"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see the ERN number ending in 43 in the top right corner?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have that document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read out paragraph 3. Please read it out loud so the interpreters can interpret it. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At around 0900 hours from our military police, we received a report that there had been an attack on probably the commander of the HVO Zenica in Pobrezje (Trokuce), at which time four people were killed (three members of the HVO and one civilian). A commander of the Zenica HVO was kidnapped and most likely wounded in the act. Authorities were given to the military police of the 3rd Corps to - together with the military police of HVO Zenica - resolve the case urgently. Official statements were issued for the public."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is an excerpt from a diary, and do you read it or do you interpret it to mean that action was carried out immediately upon learning of the kidnapping and that together with the members of the HVO the 3rd Corps took action in order to shed light on the kidnapping of Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on what I've read, I concluded that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I have just one more topic that I would like to discuss with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like us to turn -- to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in view of what you have testified about so far, were you informed enough of the situation within the 3rd Corps and did you do your best to get -- to learn everything that was to be learned about the orders and what was going on in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you see those documents back in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I did not see those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you gave evidence saying that you were able to experience yourself what the practice was of the HVO in Bosnia. Is that what you stated before the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Kordic case you gave several statements about how the policy was presented by Kordic and how he expressed the goals of the HVO in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Did you testify about that in the Kordic case?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and especially regarding Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a specific case in which this was clearly shown, this opinion and these goals. When asked by Prosecutor Nice, you mentioned the speech you heard in early 1992. Can you tell us more about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that. That was a videotape and I saw it. The videotape had footage of Dario Kordic's speech. I wasn't present at the time. That was in early 1992, but I did see the footage of his speech on that videotape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, were the goals of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna expressed during that speech and were those the goals that you experienced yourself, as you have stated, when the documents were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Prosecutor rose but I'm going to interrupt him. I see no link whatsoever between your question and the facts you're putting to us. You probably and certainly have a goal, but tell us about it because you've been going on about it for ten minutes, and personally I can't -- I fail to see the use is of it all. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Our objection, Mr. President, would actually go to the relevance, but also more importantly from our point of view, this does not arise in any shape or form from the cross-examination of this witness. We've gone way outside the scope of the indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, I anticipated on what Mr. Mundis was going to say, but you must have a good reason. If so, tell it to us because we can't follow you. If you keep putting questions that are absolutely of no use, it is a waste of time for everybody involved. Please explain the purpose of your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we go into closed session please then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General is it your personal experience from 1992 and 1993 that the HVO introduced parallel organs of authority in that area?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learned about that personally and as I stated I could personally feel the effects of that, I could feel it on my own skin, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO cause conflicts and block the BH army at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through those activities, were you able to see for yourself that the goals, as stated by Kordic and as mentioned by you in the Kordic case, were being implemented?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In both other case -- in both cases I testified about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, regardless of what you testified about in which case, please tell us, when all of the documents you saw during this case were shown to you, can you tell us what were the main causes of the conflict with HVO in Central Bosnia? Did the BH army contribute to the eruption of that conflict in any way?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information dating from 1992 and 1993, my personal experience and what happened to me personally in the field at the time, everything that I learned about it at the time I stated back then and I can confirm that now, especially having seen the HVO documents here during this trial, it is my firm belief that the cause of the conflict in Central Bosnia can be found in the policies of the HDZ implemented in the Central Bosnia territory. I already spoke about that during my testimony and I can give you more information about specific individual cases. I believe I've already testified quite in detail about this, but if the Chamber needs any more information, I'm prepared to provide it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It's now half past 3.00. We're going to have a break. Thereafter, if the other counsel want to take the floor, they can have the floor, then the Judges will put their questions. You're going to have half an hour to have a rest. Is that enough, or do you need some more time, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel fine, and half an hour should be enough for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now turning to the other counsel. Do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have just a few very specific questions for this witness. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, to the question from my learned friend from the Prosecution -- to a question -- can you hear me now? Can you hear me, General? To a question put by my learned friend the Prosecution, you gave evidence that on the 14th of April you visited Ravno Rostovo.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ravno Rostovo, as far as I understood you, is a location that holds only one motel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made that tour together with Mr. Nakic and representatives of the international community. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, were you given the possibility to tour the entire motel including all the premises in Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were enabled to inspect all the premises in Ravno Rostovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
