utterances.text: The officer you met there unquestioningly enabled you to do so. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood well your testimony, you came to Rostovo unannounced. There was no prior announcement that you would be coming. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We came unannounced. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to another question by the Prosecutor, you said you met an officer from the 7th Muslim Brigade and you talked to him.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said indeed he was the highest-ranking officer there and that he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend suggested to you that you met in fact the commander of the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade named Ramo Durmis.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor indeed asked me that and I answered by saying that the officer who introduced himself to me as a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade told me he was commander of the 1st Company, 1st Battalion, without mentioning his name [as interpreted]. And even if he mentioned it, he certainly didn't say Ramo Durmis, and that's what I said to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, General, that in Aril 1993 Ramo Durmis was not a member of the Muslim Brigade at all?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Mr. Ramo Durmis, and that's what I said to the Prosecution. I don't know all the members of a brigade, and it's not my mission to know them. That applies to the 7th Muslim Brigade as well. I know the commander; in some instances I know even battalion commanders, but I can't know all the soldiers of the 3rd Corps, and that's what I said to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is one error in the transcript page 95, line 14 it says Ramo Durmis wasn't a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you would allow me, I would like to ask one more question about Ramo Durmis, although the witness said he didn't know him. But since the Prosecution opened this door I would like to ask for your permission to put the question anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if I tell you that the Defence of Mr. Kubura on the 15th of November, 2004, received from the Prosecution according to Rule 68 the witness statement of Ramo Durmis given before the higher court in Zenica given on the 26th of October, 1993; that he signed to the effect that after the end of March or beginning of April he was a member of the 7th Brigade. It transpires that you were not able to meet him on the 14th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first time I'm hearing such precise information. I was not aware of it before. I only claimed that I did not know the man, Ramo Durmis. And I claimed I did not know personally soldiers within a brigade. I don't know what Ramo Durmis stated and what he signed. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one correction to the transcript. When I was putting this question, speaking about this statement, he said that he was not a member of the 7th Brigade. And it is recorded to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you be more specific for the Defence. Was he or was he not? It's not very clear, you see. What does the Defence say, that he was no longer a member or that he was a member?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The argument of the Defence, according to the statement given by Ramo Durmis himself, a signed statement, he was not a member of the 7th Brigade in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, General, the person you saw at the motel, did you know his name or not because mention is made of Ramo Durmis, the officer who introduced himself to you who was the highest-ranking officer. Did he say, My name is Ramo Durmis, or didn't he state his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have already stated that there is a possibility that he mentioned his name, but I assert he didn't say, My name is Ramo Durmis. Because when given a name, I would remember it. Maybe it was another name. In any case, I didn't hear him saying "Ramo Durmis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General, for this clarification. I would like to move now to another topic that you have also been questioned about by the Prosecution, that is the meeting in Biljesevo on the 23rd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the witness to be shown P429 again, with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the famous document we saw yesterday, the one that gave rise to translation problems.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document P429.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you before that. Now this document has been shown to you. It's DH165. I don't have to show it to you again because you commented upon it. It's a report from the commander of the 3rd Corps submitted to the superior command raising the issue of the presence of foreigners in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps dated 13th June, 1993. And that's a problem raised by Enver Hadzihasanovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the document; it was shown to me in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that the headquarters of the supreme command on the 16th of June, 1993, reacting to this report from the commander of the 3rd Corps issued an order, document DH162, item 2, regarding these foreigners, that this unit should be sent to Igman and resubordinated to a unit in Cukle. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was shown to me also in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like you to look again at something Mr. Kubura said at the meeting of the 23rd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the document was DH165.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you see this order from the superior command headquarters regarding these groups and the problem earlier pointed out by General Hadzihasanovic as well as what Mr. Kubura said at the meeting, can we conclude that what was said at the meeting is exactly the same as what Rasim Delic, headquarters commander, ordered regarding this issue set in a general context?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you talk about Mount Igman, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that when you wrote -- when you read what Kubura said at this meeting, he didn't speak of the problem as a problem of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the presence of foreigners; he spoke about it as a problem that had been pointed out earlier, as existing in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what we can read here, Mr. Amir Kubura is not saying they are engaged in his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question on this subject. Did officers and commanders attending this meeting know about the order from the headquarters of the superior command from Rasim Delic on how to deal with the problem of the foreigners?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the commander of the 3rd Corps in item 1 of the agenda said -- stated what was being done to deal with the problem of the foreigners present in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Just one more question. It was put to you by my colleague from the Prosecution and it had to do with Mr. Kubura. Do you know that when Mr. Kubura returned to Bosnia and Herzegovina he was a member of the Territorial Defence of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the Territorial Defence of what.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have this information but I later learned that he joined indeed the Territorial Defence of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the autumn of 1993 [as interpreted] he was commander of the 333rd Battalion in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that detail now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have, Mr. President, two new documents relating to the position of Mr. Kubura that he held in this period in 1992/1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but it might be necessary for the witness to add something to line 3 of page 100. When Mr. Kubura returned to Bosnia, he became a member of the Territorial Defence of -- and then we have something that was not put into the transcript. Is there a place, a particular place?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Territorial Defence of Kakanj municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kakanj, I see. Fine. Yes, do introduce the two documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: For "the autumn of 1993" in line 10, page 100, it should be autumn of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are new documents, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are new documents, Mr. President. One document was received by the Defence when searching the archives of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the other document dated 6th August is one originating from the Sarajevo collection. Just one correction before that in the transcript. When I was asking my question that he was a member of the 333rd Brigade, it was in the late autumn of 1992, not 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this document, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this one document. It's from the republic headquarters of supreme command of the 6th of August. Is that the one you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look first at the first document of the 11th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see from this document that Mr. Kubura in -- was first placed in the position of assistant chief of staff for operations and training in the 7th Brigade according to establishment.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order of the 3rd Corps from the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Kubura by virtue of an order of 1993 became the chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date when Mr. Amir Kubura was appointed chief of staff of the 3th Muslim Brigade. I cannot remember that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was acting commander as of the 1st of April until 8th of August, 1993, in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that he was acting commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please now look at the second document dated 8th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen the document. You mean the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake, 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say -- it says on my paper 06/08/93. Is that the one you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was signed by the chief of staff of the supreme commander Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that Mr. Kubura was commander of the 7th Brigade from the 6th of August 1993 until March of 1994, that is less than 8 months?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date when he ceased to be commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but I know that he didn't spend long in that position. That much I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked with him during the war, with Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you characterise your cooperation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As second highest-ranking in the corps, I can say that we had a very successful cooperation. Mr. Kubura was very cooperative as a superior commander and he always complied with the orders of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having seen these documents, it was shown to you that he was first in the Territorial Defence and then in the 333rd Brigade. I can tell you that Mr. Kubura was never a member of the Muslim forces that were mentioned over these past few days.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that he was. I had no knowledge of who was and who wasn't a member of Muslim forces. I believe that Amir Kubura has never been outside the system of control and command. If he was a member of the TO, then he couldn't have been a member of the Muslim forces because Muslim forces were never within the composition of the Territorial Defence. I can state that with full responsibility before this Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The time has come for the three Judges who are in charge of you to put questions. I shall be the first one to put questions to you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the first place at the very beginning of your testimony you had stated that you had testified before a domestic court. Could you tell me when you did so and where.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified in November 1994 before the district court -- sorry, cantonal court of the joint Doboj canton in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. Either the witness made a slip of the tongue or it's a transcript error. Can he repeat when he testified. It says "1994" here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was it 1994 or 2004?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my slip of the tongue, Your Honours. It was in 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 2004, this is very recent. It goes back to only a few weeks. You testified before one Judge or several Judges? Who did you testify before?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had before me several people sitting next to the judge who was questioning me. I couldn't tell you whether it was a panel of judges or a jury, but they told me that it was part of the cantonal judiciary. That's what they told me. I didn't ask about any details. I saw before me a number of people. On one side sat the defence, on the other side sat the prosecution. And before me there were judges. I don't know if all of them were judges or some of them were jurymen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there one accused or was there no accused when you testified?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accused was there, Edin Hakanovic. He was sitting in the same room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what were the questions about? Were the questions put to you the same as those put here? Or they were more focused on a specific item, topic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The questions concerned my level of knowledge about the event in Dusina, but they were much shorter than the questions asked here. And as I understood, they sought much less detail than is sought here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as far as you know, this Edin Hakanovic, what is his connection with the event in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Court asked me if I knew Mr. Edin Hakanovic. I answered I had never seen him before, that I was seeing him for the first time. But I also told the Court what I knew about the events in Dusina village of the 26th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, what is he charged with, this Mr. Edin Hakanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was told, he was charged with the murder of soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, at the very beginning -- yes, yes, Mrs. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us. Just wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I want to know something. You explained to us that you first were in charge of the Defence of the territory in Zenica and then you were appointed assistant to the commander of the 3rd Corps. I'd like to know this: Until when were you the assistant to the commander? Because we know that General Hadzihasanovic ceased to be the commander on the 1st of November. So who was he replaced by in the 3rd Corps? And then you remember, number two, until when [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will answer your first question. After the departure of General Enver Hadzihasanovic and his moving to a higher post in the Main Staff of the BH army, the commander of the 3rd Corps became the late general Mehmed Alagic; that was your first question. Your second question had to do how long did I stay on the post of the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. I can tell you that I remained in that post until February of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So after February 1995, what did you do? Because this question was never asked, and I would like to know what you did after February 1995.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After leaving my post of deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, I became chief of the administration for military education within the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was this? Until when? And in -- with which rank?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The seat of that administration was in Sarajevo, and some offices were in Zenica, fewer offices. The main bulk of offices was in Sarajevo. At the time, I had the rank of the brigadier of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you were in this position until which year?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date or the year. All I can say right now is that I left that post and moved to the Ministry of Defence when I became deputy assistant to the minister in charge of inspections. I cannot recall what year that was, but that was the post that I was transferred to after being chief of military education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were the deputy to the general in charge of inspections. Was this your last post before you retired?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite, Your Honour. I can tell you this very accurately because in my notes I have the dates of my various posts. I hope you will understand should I make an error in giving you all these dates. In our next break I can check my notes and then I will be sure to give you precise dates. Now to answer your question. After that position as deputy assistant to the minister for inspections within the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I moved to the position of the deputy minister in charge of personnel appointments, and that was my last military post. And in year 2000, I retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand you correctly, you now receive a pension and you have been receiving a pension for four years; you have no other activity, no other work?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I've been retired for four years now, and I'm not involved in any activities right now. I believe now I need to rest because I've been through a lot during wartime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your explanation. Yesterday the Prosecution presented to you a notepad, green-coloured notepad, which was the log, the operational log, and you said you never seen the documents. I want to know one thing: When you were the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps in Zenica, did you have an office; and if so, where was the office?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 3rd Corps was housed in a building. I had my office right next to the office of the corps commander; that was a small room which had just a desk. And this is where I spent my time when discharging my duties within the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have a secretary, a soldier who was acting as secretary? Did you have some sort of secretarial staff? Because you were the deputy commander of corps of 30.000 men. Did you have a secretary?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 3rd Corps we had no secretaries. We had no secretariat. We had female or male persons who did the telephone duty and made connection through the switchboard, telephone switchboard. These people normally sat in front of the office where I was and where was the command of the 3rd Corps. That was not the secretary in a typical sense, as one might perceive the role of a secretary. I've already been asked this in relation to Mr. Mamhi [phoen] Sakib and at that time I replied that there were no secretaries in the 3rd Corps, at least not in the traditional sense of that word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your office did you have a telephone? Did you have a personal telephone number? Indeed, we have a document with the telephone numbers. Did you have a telephone set? Could you be reached on a personal line, direct line?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember right now whether I had a direct line or not, but at any rate the calls were made through the switchboard. And there was a person who operated the switchboard sitting in front of the office. Anybody who wanted to enter my office had to announce themselves to the person sitting in front of my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you were the deputy commander, did you have a fax machine?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In my office we did not have a fax. The fax machine was in the operations centre. So if I needed to use the fax, then it had to go through the operations centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw that you signed documents from the municipal defence, from the TO district. The TO district and the premises were where in Zenica? Were they somewhere else than the premises of the 3rd Corps? I mean in physical terms.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot recall ever signing a document of the municipal TO staff. I was never commander of the municipal TO staff, Your Honour, but I was a commander of the district staff; and that's quite a different matter within the command and control system. Perhaps this is some error, but I never, ever signed a document of the municipal TO staff in any municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were the commander -- the district commander for the municipal TO. And this district of the municipal TO staff, did it have premises?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was a commander of the district TO staff before I became deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. The premises of the district TO staff for the Zenica region or district were housed in an entirely different building; they were not even close, although both were located in the city of Zenica but quite at a distance from each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in that building, in those premises, did you have an office, a telephone, a secretary?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As commander of the district TO staff, while I held that position I worked in the building where the command of the district TO staff in Zenica was housed. And when I became deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, then I moved to the building where the 3rd Corps headquarters was located. And I didn't go anymore to the building where the district TO staff was located. Now that you're asking me about my office at the time, when I was commander of the district TO staff for Zenica, I can tell you that, yes, I did have an office. And in front of that office, once again, there was a person who we called secretary, but not in the tradition sense of the word. Because in the district TO staff we did not have any secretarial positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, what I wanted to know is this: In January 1993, didn't you have two offices, one office in the 3rd Corps, the other being in the district TO staff? And to be more precise, on the 26th of January, 1993, did you not have two offices? I'm very specific there, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. In January of 1993 I did not have two offices. Your Honours, I wish to reiterate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, can I have Exhibit P200. Can I see the text in B/C/S? Mr. Usher, please put the document on the ELMO. You can see this document from the district Defence staff on the 26th of January. It is sent to the duty operations officer in the 3rd Corps. The title is in English: "Regular report as of 1800 hours." If you turn over to the next page, you see your name with a signature. Were you the one who signed? And if you weren't, who signed it? And why do we find your name on this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shown by you is something that I have right in front of me now. I've already explained this situation here before the Trial Chamber. This was at the time when we had a transition and when the 3rd Corps was just being established. Your Honours, this is not my signature here; this is a signature of a person acting as commander of the district defence staff in Zenica before it ceased to exist. I explained here quite in detail about this, as there were a lot of questions put to me. And I explained that this was a transitional period before the district TO staff for Zenica was shut down. So this document was signed by a person who was acting as commander. At the time, Your Honours, I did not have a dual role.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. However, the signatory signs on your behalf, doesn't he? And for the men signing, he signs on your behalf for you because you are the commander of the district defence staff on the 26th of January. Otherwise, if it wasn't the case, he would have put his name. But we see your name. Therefore, you are the one who is responsible, who is in charge. After all, the army is not everything, it is specific in the army. The one signing knows who he is signing for. Admittedly there was a transitional stage, but on the 26th of January the district defence staff still existed, didn't it? And you failed to understand why your name is used. Is that what you are telling us? How do you account for this? We need to have a consistent explanation.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've tried to explain that earlier. At the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you explained this. However, I'm asking you a question, a very specific question as a judge. How do you account for somebody who is in a chain of command should sign a document on your behalf? Either it is a mistake by the one who signs, that may be the case. Or -- how do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if there was the acting commander here, then the name of that person would have been here. However, this document is signed by the commander. Therefore, Your Honours, I can assure you that at the time I held only one office. I did not have simultaneously two posts, both deputy commander of the 3rd Corps and commander of the district Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm going thereby even more specific in my next question. Are you the author of the document? Do you regard yourself as the author of the document, I mean the contents thereof?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not the author of this document. I also cannot say that I stand by this document, because at the time the district TO staff was properly functioning and there was person who acted as commander. Perhaps the person who prepared the document wasn't quite clear about these two different functions; that is a possibility. I do allow that possibility. And as I've always claimed before this Honourable Chamber, whenever I was 100 per cent sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we have a whole series of documents which you signed on behalf of General Hadzihasanovic. We have documents where your signature can be found on behalf of General Hadzihasanovic. So somebody signing for a higher authority knows what they're doing. So when you signed on behalf of General Hadzihasanovic we can only but suppose that the one signing for you also knows that he's doing.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to give a very detailed explanation here in order to clarify this for Your Honours. When these high posts are involved as well as the high posts I held within the 3rd Corps, the order always had to be signed by the supreme command staff. And I've already explained to you about the process. I explained that the links were not the traditional links that exist in all other armies. We were in the middle of the war. We were completely isolated. We were in Zenica. And the communications were disrupted. So this process of sending orders from the supreme staff -- from the supreme command to Zenica and then back was quite a laborious one. Your Honours, you have to analyse the situation as it was at the time, at the time when these documents were produced. You should not analyse the situation as it is now, when the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is quite an orderly institution. At the time when I was informed that I was to become deputy commander of the 3rd Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to stop there. I mean, we're moving to something else, but I'll come back to this document later on. I just want to move on to another topic. You talked about arms. You said so, but you're not the only one in saying so, you told us that the ABiH found itself in a very difficult situation regarding weapons. Witnesses have come to tell us that the Territorial Defence which under the old regime of the JNA received the weapons from the JNA -- well, when the JNA withdrew, the TO took over the weapons and we were even told that the Travnik barracks were bombed to recover the weapons. So from what you told us but also what other witnesses told us, you were underequipped in terms of weaponry. Can you confirm this or is it not so? Or does this have to be seen in relative terms?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can confirm that we were very, very ill-equipped in terms of weaponry and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not taken some documents now, but I could have taken some documents showing unit by unit how each unit was equipped. And even if you were underequipped, underarmed, you had mortars, you had automatic rifles, machine-guns. You even had helicopters. You had armoured materiel as well, armoured vehicles. So where did all this materiel come from, as far as you know? Where did it come from? How did it get to you? How did you manage little by little to set up all this materiel? Because as you explained there were two front lines; you had the Serbs and the HVO. So if you had front lines, you had fighting. If there was fighting, you used weaponry. Where did the weaponry come from? I'm saying "weaponry." It can be also transmissions, communications materiel, it can be clothing, whatever. So where did it all come from?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can speak about this at length, but I will try as briefly as possible to explain this to you so that you can understand the situation as it developed. Speaking of weaponry and supplies I can tell you that people used water-supply pipes to make rifles to shoot. I can tell you that the brigade we set up was supposed to have 100 tanks; it had three instead. And those three were of very old types that had been left behind in the barracks as obsolete, useless. And people made them usable again with the help of some companies. They didn't have good aiming devices. All this equipment was left behind as obsolete. Later on we when received some equipment [as interpreted], but in the early stages, this is how we obtained weaponry. In addition to that, there was the black market and people purchased weapons through very channels. I have information, for instance, that some individuals bought weapons from the HVO. You will certainly know, Your Honours, that in war the black market thrives and a lot of dealings go on. Speaking of communications, we did not have proper communications in the 3rd Corps. If you speak about clothing, our troops did not have proper clothing. On Mount Vlasic we had people wearing sneakers of temperatures of minus 20 degrees, but that only speaks about the courage of the people fighting for the homeland.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 119, line 8, it says: "We later received some equipment." The witness actually said "captured" and I would like this corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Initially you are from the navy; that's where you were first. And you later found yourself among the ground forces. Being trained as an officer, did you learn of the existence of the JNA manual of the ground forces, JNA ground forces? It was created in 1990. It was supposed to be revised and published in 1992 but given -- because of the events it didn't really come into being. Are you aware of the existence of JNA ground forces manuals?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the former JNA I had occasion to familiarise myself with many rules of the former JNA on the use of units. I don't know which particular unit you have in mind, but I have to tell you that although a naval officer myself, in some tactical drills and even operation drills, I participated as an officer of the ground forces. Within our system of schooling, it was a principle we observed in the JNA. So the rules of the ground forces were not foreign to me. But I was not an expert in that area. However, when I finished the staff officers' school --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give you a definition in paragraph 63 of the manual which was supposed to be the book of authority in all the units of the former Yugoslav. "Command and control of the armies is to be exerted through planning, coordination, command and control, preparing and carrying out the operations and actions in connection with fighting." This is the definition I wanted to give you. Do you agree to know what is command and control of the army, because I'm reading there one of the provisions of this book which was the authoritative manual in the former Yugoslavia. Do you agree with this definition?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I studied the rules that were in use before I left the JNA, which was in 1991. And until 1991, I had occasion to read the rules speaking to the system of command and control. I cannot remember any longer those rules, but if you quoted from the proper paragraph of that rule I have no reason to disbelieve that it is indeed the paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I carry on. Regarding command responsibility, the following is said in paragraph 65 of the said manual: "The corps commander is responsible for carrying out the mission. He makes decisions, gives orders to subordinates, organises cooperation and coordination of actions and controls to make sure that decisions are carried out." Do you agree with this definition of what the role is of a corps commander?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really have to clarify this. I said I left the former JNA in 1991. At that time within the organisation of the JNA we had no such units, and I was never in the role of the corps commander in the former JNA. That's one thing. Another thing: Your Honours, the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not simply copy those rules and adopt them as its own. So we cannot speak about the application of JNA rules without any change --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. It is recorded. Could you tell us, because after all you were the number two in the 3rd Corps and so you experienced action and as much as your office was there and was not to be found in the premises of the municipal defence staff, so basically you can break down military action in two periods, offensive or defensive periods. At the level of the 3rd Corps, when was an action a defensive one or an offensive one? And depending on that, was there a preparatory meeting where people convened to the meeting in writing and was the invitation sent to subordinate levels by the top command? Was there a meeting, either to prepare an action or to prepare a defensive action? Was there a briefing? What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I shall say that this is a very broad question. Speaking of combat operations, I completely agree with you: they can be offensive or defensive. Within that global division, there are subcategories of defensive and offensive operations depending on the level in tactical, strategic and operative terms. We can have a lengthy discussion of this. Certainly, at the command of the 3rd Corps at this stage when it was being established was unable for a long time to organise any offensive operation of any operative significance; we only engaged in defensive actions at that stage of organisation of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So at this stage, as you told us - and you're still under oath, I'll remind you of that - as far as you know there were never any offensive actions; you only experienced defensive operations and actions. Is that what you're telling us? You said you were going to say -- tell the truth and nothing but the truth, and just a moment ago you told us that you only had defensive actions. So I'm putting the question to you in order to avoid any misunderstanding. You were only aware of defensive actions?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm speaking about particular time period, namely the time when the 3rd Corps was being established. At that time we were not capable of mounting a traditional offensive operation. I can state that with full responsibility. In later stages of the war, the corps did mount offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From which month onwards? From which year onwards did it mount such operations?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, since you expect from me a very precise definition of defensive versus offensive operation - and I really want you to follow me precisely - for defensive or offensive operations, one needs to collect adequate equipment, be it personnel, equipment, or logistics. We are talking about vast resources. We can talk about lower-level, tactical, or defensive actions. If I now defined operative versus tactical combat operations, I can tell you that in 1993 the 3rd Corps did not have enough resources or men to organise an offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in 1993 the 3rd Corps did not mount any offensive operations, not a single one; is that right, according to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know how this is being interpreted to you in English or in French. I can hear very well what I'm being told in B/C/S. I'm speaking about operations led by the corps. And what I get back is "actions." There is a huge difference between "action" and "operation," and I would like to avoid being seen as somebody who's not telling the truth just because of wrong interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is like, you know, toying with words. This is not the first time. We're talking about the 3rd Corps in which you were the number two man. This 3rd Corps, did it in 1993 mount any offensive? Of course to do so, as you said, you need logistics, you need the personnel, you've got the assess the situation; I agree. But I'm putting this to you: You were number two in the 3rd Corps. Did the 3rd Corps at any time in 1993 find itself in a situation where it could mount an offensive or did this corps do nothing but defend itself in 1993 on the front line? Please be -- don't play with words. I have a good reason for putting this question to you. I repeat it: In 1993 did the 3rd Corps at any point of 1993 envisage such an offensive action and did it have the means to do so at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I state with full responsibility that we have to be very precise here in stating what we understand by operations. I don't understand what you mean by "operations" or "actions." If you mean some actions the 3rd Corps did mount offensive actions of some kind in 1993. Those were actions of lesser importance, maybe tactical operative importance, but certainly not operative importance. I want to be precise. I don't know how this that I'm saying is being interpreted to you; I don't know what type of interpretation you're getting. But I'm saying there had been offensive actions in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps at some point in 1993. Now we can go stage by stage, period by period within that year and I can explain in even greater detail. But I'm saying in 1993 there were offensive actions within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. Yes, I can say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When there is an offensive or defensive action, the command, be it the chief of staff, the number one man or number two, do the chief officers get together to discuss the matter to see how feasible it is in order to plan the day when the attack is to be mounted? Does all this happen or is it just merely empirical? You were in the field; what can you tell us as to the way this type of operation was prepared.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm getting some misinterpretation again. I was speaking about actions and the interpreter is talking back to me about operations. I hope you can intervene. The interpreter is again mentioning operations to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to make it clear to you. There are quite a few of us here in this courtroom who were in the army. In the army either you are on a line awaiting an attack or you attack; one of the two things. Either you are on the defensive or you are on the offensive. My question speaking of operations or action is: Like, you move away from your line in order to gain ground from the enemy. Do you understand this? If, for instance, you have a coordinate 852 on a map and you want to get hold of the position, is this a defensive or an offensive action?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have just lent me great assistance in answering your question because I see now that you are speaking about any kind of action, combat action or operation. And I can answer your future questions. Speaking of an offensive combat action, of course preparations are necessary and they are indeed undertaken. In the event of defensive combat actions or operations, preparations again are carried out but to a lesser extent. Defensive operations require less time and less resources than offensive operations, which require much greater resources because the expenditures are much greater. You have to make artillery preparations and other necessary preparations before the troops actually go into operative action. And I would appreciate it when the interpreter is interpreting that they shouldn't say "operations," that they should say operative actions; that's what I meant. And when you mentioned, for instance, a trig point or an elevation, when you interpret this it can be an attack; but it can also be -- sorry, it can also be an offensive defence. If you have a line that you firmly hold and the enemy takes a small elevation, a small feature, and you want to recapture it, to have it under your control again, then that is called offensive defence. You are actually improving your tactical position in defence. You are not carrying out attack operations, offensive operations even though you did recapture this elevation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By way of an example you stated yourself when you were standing in front of the map you mentioned the crossroads, the Lasva crossroads and you said it was a well-known location as a strategic location. When the military are in Lasva, when they make a move, they leave this famous crossroads in order to move to trig point 852, which is above a given village. Now in your view, is this an offensive action or is it a an offensive -- defensive one? I mean, it's hard to follow you. So when there is a movement, when these people left this famous crossroads in order to occupy trig point 852, how do you qualify this action?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if at that trig point you are just speaking about the enemy used to be, and if prior to that that trig point had never before been under the control of, say, the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, then we can call it an offensive action. If, on the contrary, that trig point was under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina first and then it had to be abandoned due to enemy action, in that case recapturing of that trig point would qualify as offensive defence because you are just recapturing your defence line that you used to hold before the enemy took it away from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a very exact answer. Thank you. In this type of a situation, so either you attack or you defend because you want to recapture, at the level of the 3rd Corps, is there a watch system being set up? The duty officer, does he have this type of operations and where does he have to warn the 3rd Corps commander, the chief, or yourself? How does it work in practice? I mean the connection between the field and the command, of course. And the reason why I mention the JNA manual, everything is set out, the information must go back -- from the field to -- upwards. In your experience, did you have -- was there such a communication path from the ground upwards?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am getting wrong interpretation again. I hear the word "operation" again. Please, Your Honour, I have already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In an offensive action if the 3rd Corps mounts an attack, the people on the ground, do they have to forward the information upwards to the level of the 3rd Corps of the headquarters? Do they have some duty service there so that the action on the ground can be monitored? Because in all military manuals it is explained how it should work. So I want to know whether you did the same, as in the books.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're talking about a tactical offensive combat action, those are -- rather, offensive actions of lesser significance, minor offensive actions. The commander of course is interested in every action in his area of responsibility involving his personnel, but if those offensive actions are carried out on the tactical level then the operations duty officer, who was on duty 24 hours a day in the headquarters, then he gets information that offensive tactical actions are taking place at that trig point, but it [as interpreted] doesn't necessarily have to alarm the commander who may be involved in a different mission. If those offensive combat actions are on a larger scale, the operations duty officer would again receive appropriate information from the ground, both in theory and in practice. But you have to bear in mind that in practice communications often failed. We had very poor communications equipment, and I know of situations, real situations that happened, Your Honours, when combat actions of tactical significance were taking place, offensive combat actions of tactical significance, we were sometimes not able to get that information from the operations duty officer. Sometimes we got it with a delay, and that was the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you got the information with a delay, did you do everything that needed to be done at the level of the 3rd Corps in order to achieve the result, which is either to assess the loss incurred or the enemy loss? Was it being done systemically in the 3rd Corps? When soldiers were killed, for instance, 3rd Corps soldiers, did you see this feedback as fast as possible? As far as you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of when the information of the ground reaches the corps command, whether it arrives there on time or with a delay, if a large human loss is involved then alarm is raised within the corps. Naturally the corps commander is informed in detail or will be informed about that specific situation involving significant human loss. The corps command will definitely react to such information once it receives it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know regarding a loss of life, how or at what level does the corps -- 3rd Corps commander react? When there is one person killed or ten or 100? When or how does the 3rd Corps commander react? From your experience, of course.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already testified about that, saying that a commander cannot remain indifferent when even one soldier is killed. The question is: What can a commander do if one soldier is killed? If ten soldiers are killed in a certain time interval or a short space of time, then that is quite worrisome for the commander of the corps. If 100 soldiers are killed in a short space of time, then that is a catastrophe. I don't know if I was clear enough giving these figures. I don't know if that was enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you were. As far as you know, during 1993 how many soldiers were killed within the 3rd Corps involving all units? We have documents, but I'm asking your assessment. We have figures, but I want you to tell me so. On the basis of what you know, you incurred how many losses?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is very difficult for me to answer this question. I don't know what losses were suffered in 1993 in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps in all units. This is a very difficult question for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know? You can't even give us a vague amount, an approximate number?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite all my best efforts to answer all of your questions, Your Honours, it is very difficult to answer this particular question. It's not that I'm avoiding answering this question, Your Honour, I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Now it's 5 past -- it's 25 to 6.00. We'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. General, before the break we were speaking about the number of soldiers killed and you said you didn't have any figures. There is a report from the 3rd Corps, but there is no point showing this report to you otherwise we're going to waste more time. It's dated the 23rd of August, 1993, and it records the number of soldiers wounded and injured until the 31st of July, 1993. We have 1.570 killed and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the number of injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 7th Brigade has -- records 60 killed and 274 wounded, for your information. I'm asking your view on this. The municipal defence staff of Zenica records 32 killed and 58 wounded. This is document P192. Do these figures seem correct to you? What do you think.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have checked my notes during the break and I can give you the precise dates of my various posts that I spoke of earlier. I have the exact dates with me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We'll get back to that later on. Regarding the number of people killed, do the figures I just gave you, do they seem in keeping with what you learned on the ground? By the way, in the transcript it is on page 130, line 24. I'm giving you the figure that was not recorded. 1570 killed, which is a major figure. You were not aware of this? Curiously enough, General, anything having to do closely with the 3rd Corps seems to be something you're never aware of. This famous operations log, you don't know anything about it. And another important figure is something that you don't know either. Could you explain this to us. Why don't you know this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know -- I knew that we had significant losses, and this is quite understandable. I simply said to you that I did not know the figure. The losses were quite high, the losses of the 3rd Corps because the 3rd Corps was poorly equipped. We did not have the artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to show you another document. Mr. Registrar, can you please give us Exhibit 120 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is -- concerns somebody who died in Dusina on the 26th of January and several people who were wounded on that same date in Dusina. This is P720. You're going to have a look at this, the document, in your own language and I'm going to seek some comments from you. It can be put on the ELMO so that everybody can have a look at it. You can see this document now. Apparently it is sent by a social worker. I suppose that is the 7th Brigade. Who was this sent to? Look in the bottom left corner. What can you read in the bottom left corner? Who are the addressees of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can see here that it says it was forwarded -- one copy was forwarded to the municipal defence staff in Zenica; the second copy was forwarded to the Islamic Centre in Zenica; and one copy was sent to the archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you confirm that this document is of a military origin, since there is a stamp on the right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It says here "military unit number" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the link between the army and the Islamic centre? Why is a statement on the number of wounded and killed is being sent to the Islamic Centre? I'd like to know that. Can you give us an explanation, since this is something I can see here right now.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know why this document was sent to the Islamic Centre in Zenica. I couldn't give you an answer to this. Perhaps we should ask the person who signed this document. Now, again you're going to say I know nothing but I have an explanation: I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have no explanation. Let's move on to another topic. Mr. Registrar, I'm going to need a few documents. We first need Exhibit P431. Before giving this document, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Open session. Witness, please look at P148. You're going to receive the B/C/S version and I'll keep the English one. This document has been translated into your language. It comes from the ECMM. It is a daily operational report dated 25th of April, 1993. Point C is an account of what happened in the village of Miletici. Please read it out. "Mention is made by an eyewitness of the fact that 15 individuals of Islamic type dressed in ordinary uniform surrounded the village at 1500 hours on the 24th. A leader was called Ramadan and a few of them had police badges on their shoulders. They demanded the villagers to lay down their arms, which was refused. Five villagers were caught, whilst the other 36 escaped to a neighbouring village. The hands of the five men who were caught were tied behind their backs and they seemed to have been mistreated. One body was found in a house; the other four bodies were found somewhere else in another," so says the text. "Confirmation was done this afternoon by Mr. Eric Peterson [phoen] accompanied by Mr. Merdan, Mr. Nakic and the Brit Bat security officer." Can you tell us this: Connection is being made -- or the account that is given here, does it tally with what you learned on the ground or with the information you were given? Because you are mentioned by name.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was in Miletici at this time as is stated here. I was there together with the people mentioned in the text. I stated what I had seen in the village of Miletici. I testified about that in detail. Let me repeat now: I heard from the villagers -- not only I, but Mr. Nakic who was present -- we heard from the villagers that these murders had been committed by the mujahedin, at least this is what the villagers told us. I called them the villagers. I didn't know that they were all mixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a confusion. You were put questions by the two parties and you said that you had spoken about it to General Hadzihasanovic. Can you confirm that after you went on the spot you reported to the commander of the 3rd Corps? Did you tell the 3rd Corps commander that you'd been on the ground together with Mr. Peterson, Mr. Nakic? Did you report to him regarding this event?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, all I'm trying to say is that I did not hear any of the villagers mention the name of Ramadan. Upon returning to the 3rd Corps command, I informed the commander of the 3rd Corps about what I had seen on that day in the village of Miletici and about what I had learned from the residents of that village. This is what I informed the commander of the 3rd Corps about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you told General Hadzihasanovic, This is what we are being told? Did you tell him so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I informed General Hadzihasanovic precisely as I was informed by the villagers. I did not have any other information at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You received the information. What happened at the level of the 3rd Corps after that? You say, well, so this is what apparently happened there. In concreto, what happened? What was done? Was there an investigation? Were their villagers asked to come and tell the story? What happened precisely? As far as you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there at the spot I told the villagers that they could go back, that it was safe for them to be in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. After that. So you reported to General Hadzihasanovic in Zenica, you reported to him, because you were his deputy. So you told your superior that you went to the village, that the international observers were there. You -- they were bound to be interested. And also Mr. Nakic was present, so it was likely for the whole thing to have some echo. What happened at the level of the 3rd Corps? What was there going to happen?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I conveyed what I knew at the time, what I learned of, the information I received from the field. I told them that this had not been done by the members of the BH army but rather by the mujahedin, as the villagers called them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what you say. Fine. I'll stop there because we'll talk tomorrow about the mujahedin. We don't need this document anymore. Let's move on to Dusina. Mr. Registrar, can you please hand over to the witness Exhibit P346. We'll need P312 and P 131, P314, as well, as well as P200. P346 as well. Please have a look at this document. Who is the person supposed to either have drafted or have endorsed the document? Which is the name that you can see on the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as far as I can tell, this is signed by the same person as one of the other documents you showed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are therefore telling us that this document is something you're not aware of. You never saw this document. Let us admit that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You've just told the witness that he's never seen the document. That's never what he said. Mr. President, we'd like the Trial Chamber to give enough time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down, Mr. Bourgon. The Defence is of the view that you have seen this document. They would like you to have more time to answer my question. I will put the question again to you. Have you seen this document before? Were you aware -- was it presented to you? You said no for the first document, so I thought it was the same for this one. But apparently the Defence is of the view that you have seen this document. What can you say to this? Were you appraised [as interpreted] of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, concerning the first document I only commented on the signature and my own name on it. I did not comment upon the document itself. Equally, I made the same comment on the mention of my name and the signature in this one. I said to the Honourable Court that I was aware of the reports that reached the command of the 3 Corps regarding events in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document as such, the one you can see, did you see at any point in time in January or following the 26th of January from Zenica, did you read it then or is this now the first time you are reading this document? I don't know, you see.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Since this is a document that I had earlier shown the witness and the witness explained it, he can explain again but I believe that all these documents are documents that after the meeting the Kiseljak he reviewed in order to make a report on the 27th of what their subordinated commands had done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Defence has just suggested that you may have seen this document following the Kiseljak meeting on the 27th of January. Do you share the Defence's view?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree, Your Honour, with your assumption. I was not able to see this document on the 27th. I told you that on the 26th I read a report, or rather reports that reached the command of the 3rd Corps, in order to prepare for the meeting that place the next day in Kiseljak. That's what I testified here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you say you read reports on the 26th in order to prepare for a meeting on the 27th. As far as you can remember, this document dated the 26th, could you have seen it? Could it have reached you? You see the document is sent to the 3rd Corps; you see that on the top corner. So it must have reached the highest level. You can't remember? It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The witness did not say that he didn't remember the document. He wasn't given enough time to look at it at ease without being stressed and without any hostility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit down. I do not allow you. Your question is totally inappropriate, Mr. Bourgon. I put the question to the witness asking him whether he received the document and he said he didn't because he didn't sign it. The document mentions Zenica district defence; he said it wasn't him because he wasn't there. I asked him whether he was given the document on the 26th of January and he says he didn't, unless you want to say yes now. But my question is a simple one. Regarding the contents of this document, it was not drafted in the 3rd Corps but in the district. Is there any possibility for you to have read this document then? This is the very purpose of my question. The Defence would like to give you more time, for you to have more time. Take the time you need to answer. I'm not talking about the content of the document; I'm talking about the document itself. Can you have seen the document as such at any point in time? So without getting all upset can you tell me whether you have seen the document or not or you saw the document or not rather?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am precisely trying to tell the truth all the time. I'm under oath and I'm completely aware of that. You asked me here about the signature and the title of the document. You did not allow me to comment upon the document itself. I only briefly answered your questions. If you allow me to read the contents of this document, then I will be able to tell you whether I had occasion to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, please. Look into the contents.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just read this report. I can recall and I state with full responsibility that I read all of the reports that arrived at the 3rd Corps regarding Dusina. And I assert that among the other reports I read this one, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You see -- so now you're stating that you read the report. Very good. Now you are going to be given Exhibit P312. P312. I have the English in front of me, and you have the other version. Please read the document. It is a certificate.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You will have noticed that the name of the person who was killed features in the report marked P346 of which you said that you'd read it. Here's my question: Is it usual when somebody dies in action for a delegation from his unit to be sent in order to announce the news of his death to the family? Is that -- is this what has always been done or -- in this very instance is sit something that is out of the ordinary? How did it happen when somebody was killed in action? Who was going to tell the family about the death of that person? Was it the military authority who would do that or were there colleagues of the deceased person conveying the news? Because here it is mentioned that five people were sent in order to inform the family. What can you say regarding this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, for all members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were killed, we established two, three, or more member commissions to go to the family and tell them that their loved one had lost his life in the ranks of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us see Exhibit P200. P200. Let me see the B/C/S version. Yes, please have a look at this. Look towards the end. The document is dated the 26th of January, and apparently you didn't sign it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I didn't sign this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You didn't sign this document, you say. Can you confirm that this document is sent to the duty officer, the operations duty officer of the 3rd Corps on the 26th of January at 1800 hours?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At the level of the 3rd Corps, were you made aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I knew about this document because it was a regular report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good. Towards the end it says "proposal for further engagement of our forces." And let me read the last sentence of the proposal -- or can you read it in your own language.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Proposal for further engagement of our forces. We propose that the 1st Infantry Company from the ranks of the 333rd" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that. Move on to the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The attached unit from the ranks of the 7th Muslim Brigade is grouping its men in the sector of Lasva station in order to mount a final attack against the HVO members who are concentrated in the Rajic house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what can you say about this sentence? What does it mean in military terms? It's now 6.00 on the 26th of January. It looks as though there are still HVO members in Rajic's house and the proposal is to mount a final attack. In military terms, how do you analyse the proposal?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who signed this document had this information coming from the field and he is suggesting to the command of the 3rd Corps such an engagement of the attached unit from the 7th Muslim Brigade to execute a final attack against HVO members concentrated in the Rajic house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does this mean, that on the 26th of January at 6.00 in the afternoon there was still HVO members in the house belonging to Rajic? How do you analyse this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this paper, the person who signed it has information to the effect that there are still HVO members in the Rajic house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You knowing the 3rd Corps, is that the information you knew -- you had on -- at 6.00 on the 26th of January? What was the information you had regarding this situation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said that I had read the reports that reached the command of the 3rd Corps. I probably read this one, too, that arrived at the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only two more documents; it will be quick. P314, please. Please let me see both versions. Thank you. Can you please tell us who this document is from.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you mean this document dated 28th January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued by the district defence staff of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go to the last but one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: Municipal defence staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And please read it out.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you mean under number 3 or number 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the very end of the document. Just before the sentence about morale and the sentence that says that they lost two soldiers. The paragraph just before that.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is item 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Both sides suffered losses in manpower. According to information gathered as of 28th January, 1993, HVO lost 13 soldiers and had two wounded. A total of 31 HVO members were captured, including 25 taken over by the military police who were accommodated in the penitentiary facility. And a certain number of soldiers have been taken by the soldiers of MS. Some weapons and equipment have also been seized and the largest part of them has been kept by the Muslim force members. Our side suffered a loss of two soldiers and four wounded."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
